mechanism_narrative: A sustained 6-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A UNRATE crossing above 3.5% in one month signals rising unemployment, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) despite the rate crossing, or the rate doesn't cross in subsequent periods.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (e.g., 2 consecutive months of rising FEDFUNDS), the signal triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS in tightening cycle (e.g., 2 consecutive months above previous month's increase)
failure_condition: 20-day returns not significantly negative (p>0.05) during tightening periods, or FEDFUNDS doesn't exhibit sustained increases.

mechanism_narrative: During a labor market recovery phase (UNRATE declining and PAYEMS rising for 2 months), combined signals strengthen investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE declining and PAYEMS rising for 2 months
failure_condition: 60-day returns not significantly positive (p>0.05) during the recovery phase, or the regime conditions aren't met.
